summary: Tillamook County tower lookout on Kilchis Mountain, built 1955, abandoned 1965 and removed; a hiking guide describes a former lookout site with a demolished cabin on Cedar Butte.

facts.design: 25-ft steel tower with a 7-foot (7 1/2 per one source) cab and a cabin
facts.status_note: Abandoned 1965 and removed (register description says destroyed); a hiking guide says the cabin was demolished and glass still lies at a former lookout site on Cedar Butte. No source confirms that the guide's site is this record's site; TopoQuest's 'Kilchis Lookout' is about 1.1 km from the register's coordinates

access.note: Hiking guide describes an easy trail to the former site in Tillamook State Forest, reached by Highway 6 and a gravel road to a trailhead pullout

visit.trail_note: Easy hike from a trailhead pullout off a gravel road; the guide gives driving directions via Highway 6 and Cedar Butte Road

events.note: 25-ft steel tower with a cab and cabin on the site (FFLOS, Weebly, firelookout.com)
FFLOS record gives removed in 1965; its description says destroyed in 1965

evidence.supports: tower and cab built on the site in 1955 (FFLOS)
evidence.quote: In 1955 a steel tower with a 7X7 cab and cabin were built on the site.

evidence.supports: FFLOS says the lookout was destroyed in 1965
register coordinates (N 45.572043, W 123.714798) used for the distance check to TopoQuest
firelookout.com: 25-ft steel tower, 7x7 cab and cabin, 1955; abandoned 1965; gone
evidence.quote: 1955: 25' steel tower with 7x7' cab, cabin. Abandoned 1965. Gone.

25-ft steel tower with 7 1/2 x 7 1/2 cab constructed in 1955
evidence.quote: 1955: A 25-foot steel tower with a 7 1/2 x 7 1/2 cab constructed.

evidence.supports: former lookout site on Cedar Butte trail
evidence.quote: The short Cedar Butte Trail takes hikers to a former lookout site in the western Coast Range.

evidence.quote: Views are restricted as trees have grown up since the lookout was dismantled in the early 1950s.

evidence.supports: benches at the former site; glass from demolished cabin (today)
evidence.quote: Here, at the former lookout site, there are two benches offering views west over the South Fork Kilchis valley all the way to the Pacific Ocean. Shards of glass from the demolished lookout cabin litter the site.

evidence.supports: 1918 Cedar Butte Fire scorched 40,000 acres; Tillamook Burn fires crossed the area in the 1930s and 1940s
evidence.quote: The first major recorded fire here was the 1918 Cedar Butte Fire, which scorched 40,000 acres.

evidence.quote: Kilchis Lookout is a tower located in Tillamook County, OR at N45.571229° W123.700347° (WGS84/NAD83) and at an elevation of 2647 ft MSL.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The hiking guide places a former lookout on Cedar Butte. TopoQuest lists a 'Kilchis Lookout' tower about 1.1 km from the register's coordinates (FFLOS N 45.572043 W 123.714798; TopoQuest N45.571229 W123.700347; great-circle distance about 1,128 m), at nearly the same elevation. The story does not call them one site: no source says they are the same lookout.

The guide says the lookout was dismantled in the early 1950s; FFLOS and the Weebly record give a 1955 build, abandoned or removed in 1965. Kept the register and Weebly dates because two of three sources agree; the guide's date is unexplained. The register's status field says removed in 1965 but its description says destroyed that year; the story gives both wordings.
FFLOS and firelookout.com give a 7x7 foot cab; the Weebly record gives 7 1/2 x 7 1/2. The story reports both figures.

notes_for_editor: Brief record matched the sources (1955 build, 1965 removal, 2019 registration, 25 ft height). The biggest open question is whether the Oregon Hikers' Cedar Butte lookout is this site. The TopoQuest 'Kilchis Lookout' point is about 1.1 km from the register's coordinates (an earlier draft said 11 m; that was wrong) at nearly the same elevation, so it is not a close match. The names differ and the guide's early-1950s dismantling date conflicts with the 1955 build. A check with ODF records or a local historian would settle it. No staffing or fire history for the lookout itself was found. The FFLOS photos (Howard Verschoor collection) were not downloaded, so none are added.
